meta.title: Number of watches in use in Delhi

prompt: Estimate the number of watches currently in use in Delhi.

clarifications.answer: Assume a person owns at most one watch at any time.
Watches are cheaply repaired or replaced, so treat every owned watch as in working condition.
Take Delhi's population as about 3 crore; the ~2% rural share can be ignored for simplicity.
An income-wise split works well: ownership rises with income.

common_traps: Multiplying the whole population by one flat ownership rate instead of splitting by income.
Assuming everyone owns a watch, ignoring that ownership rises with income.
Counting watches per household rather than per person, which understates the total.

anchors.1: Guesses a number, or multiplies population by a single ownership rate with no reasoning.
anchors.3: Uses a population-times-ownership chain but with one blanket ownership rate.
anchors.5: Chooses an income-wise split and ties ownership rate to income band explicitly.

anchors.1: No segmentation; one rate for all of Delhi.
anchors.3: Segments income bands but with ownership rates not clearly tied to income.
anchors.5: Splits into upper/middle/lower income with rising ownership rates (e.g. 75/50/25%).

anchors.1: Botches crore/lakh conversions or lands far outside a plausible range.
anchors.3: Reaches a number with a conversion slip, or lands just outside 1-1.8 crore.
anchors.5: Carries crore conversions cleanly and lands near 1.35 crore (1-1.8 crore).

anchors.1: States the number as final with no check.
anchors.3: Mentions a check but does not carry it through.
anchors.5: Validates the blended ownership rate (~45%) against everyday experience of who wears a watch.
